group_findings: Recommended final order: 1 stable enterprise hero with required rotating globe; 2 compact Who we are plus verified trust strip, absorbing awards; 3 strategic value plays; 4 compact five portfolios plus platform row; 5 owned software and concise accelerators; 6 client value/Why Linkfields evidence introduction; 7 approved delivery stories; 8 required eight-industry photo grid; 9 compact commercial models; 10 concise global presence; 11 optional two-card buyer insights; 12 challenge-led contact. Remove careers and social as standalone Home sections. Existing section positions in this result refer to the original JSON array; add positions refer to this proposed final order.

The desktop screenshot is 1440 × 13,695 px and mobile 390 × 24,724 px. The problem is primarily information architecture and duplicated text, not broken responsive layout. Repeated navy/ink backgrounds, spacious sections and multiple tall mobile card catalogues make scrolling monotonous. Aim for substantially less text and a materially shorter mobile journey by compacting content, not by hiding required portfolios or dropping Public Sector/Education.

Duplication is directly verified in local JSON: Home Who we are, mission/vision/stats and global presence match About; its introductory body, five-portfolio catalogue, value-play matrix and Why Linkfields match Services; Why Linkfields also matches About. Home should orient and route; About should establish identity, leadership and evidence; Services should provide taxonomy, delivery detail and commercial choices. Deck fidelity does not require copying every slide into every page.

Hero slide copy is generally deck-aligned and all six CTA destinations are relevant. Slide 2 ‘Run the core of the enterprise on connected platforms’ repeats the platforms portfolio and standalone grid; if retained, use action CTA ‘Explore enterprise platforms’. Slide 3 ‘From AI strategy to agentic AI in production’ needs an actual governed production example and can retain ‘Explore Data & AI’. Slide 4 ‘End-to-end security, from code to AI’ should not imply every security capability is proven solely by naming VajraX, VectorX and AI Governance; retain ‘Explore Cyber Security’ with supporting delivery evidence. Slide 5 ‘Software we own. Accelerators we reuse.’ is a genuine differentiator but duplicates section 4; use ‘Explore our software’. Slide 6 ‘Talent and capability centres that scale with you’ is correctly named, but ‘Talent Advisory & GCC’ is a category label rather than action; use ‘Explore teams & capability centres’. These secondary messages must not displace the stable corporate proposition or persistent contact CTA.

Home SEO is legacy offer-led copy: title ‘Global IT Services & Solutions | Linkfields Innovations’; description ‘Linkfields Innovations is a leading provider of IT services driving digital transformation and optimizing business operations. Explore our innovative solutions!’ Replace with title ‘Enterprise Technology, Software & AI | Linkfields’ and description ‘South Africa-headquartered Linkfields combines five service portfolios, proprietary software and accelerators to modernise, operate, analyse, secure and scale enterprises.’ This removes unsupported ‘leading’, filler and American ‘optimizing’. One meaningful H1 is present. The rendered canonical points to the sandbox forwarding origin; the deployment owner should configure the confirmed public production home URL before launch, not hard-code a guessed domain during this review.

The current globe already displays a full uncropped globe and respects reduced-motion preferences. Preserve these features. The home hero currently has dot navigation, swipe and hover pause, but no explicit pause or focus-pause controls. If long scrolling remains, add a compact sticky in-page navigation using the existing site pattern: Overview, Outcomes, Capabilities, Proof, Contact; keep it keyboard-accessible and usable on mobile.

Only read-only local inspection and HTTP GETs were used. Prescribed shot.py captures initially timed out; both desktop and mobile succeeded with PW_TEST_SCREENSHOT_NO_FONTS_READY=1. Screenshot files and slices are under /tmp/review/home/. The review inspected the Home JSON, global defaults, About/Services copy for duplication, rendered Home metadata and hero implementation. No builds, seeds, apply scripts, service commands or form submission were run. The parent still needs to write /home/ubuntu/linkfields/docs/review/01-home.md.
missing_content: Client-approved case studies demonstrating actual combinations of service portfolios, proprietary software and accelerators, with permission to publish client names/logos, quotations and outcomes or a clearly anonymised alternative.

Evidence register for 95%+ success, up to 6× speed, up to 40% development savings and up to 50% infrastructure savings: cohort/project, definitions, baseline, period, measurement method and source. Confirm what ‘20+ years of industry leadership experience’ measures.

Exact 2026 FT & Statista ranking evidence and correct badge; current B-BBEE Level 1 document; any renewed Great Place to Work certificate with entity, territory and validity. The visible 2023–2024 India badge cannot establish current 2026 certification.

Product demonstration material: actual UI screenshots, one clear enterprise use case per product, integrations/deployment information and confirmed independent licensing/subscription/SaaS terms. Evidence of reusable accelerator impact rather than a list of names.
A compact commercial-model entry point distinguishing the five buying models from GCC/talent engagement options, linked to the Services details.

Confirmed office/market-presence status, regional buyer contacts and legal entities; verified vendor partnership designations and their scope before displaying ‘Our Partners’. Confirm the public LinkedIn profile rather than using an administrator URL.

Current, authored, dated buyer-focused insights with valid article destinations, plus a confirmed enquiry-handling process, privacy explanation, response-time commitment if any and working sales mailbox.

group_findings: P1 — Establish one company source of truth: '(Pvt) Ltd' versus '(Pty) Ltd', 2008 founding versus leadership experience, UK versus Botswana presence, conflicting South African phone numbers and precise map pins versus verified office locations.

P2 — Home should preview; About should substantiate company identity and credibility; Our approach should detail delivery and engagement. Who we are, Global presence and Industries are exactly copied from home to About; Value plays and Industries are exactly copied to Our approach. Retain deck themes but avoid identical full blocks.

P1 — Both frontend and server enquiry validation reject non-South-African numbers. Fix internationally, make phone optional, add inline privacy context, improve message entry and confirm response/NDA promises. No form was submitted.
P1 — Replace all public LinkedIn '/admin/feed/posts/' destinations. Use one verified public recruitment route and a separate verified public company profile.

P1 — Three 2024 blogs retain expired 2022/2023 forecasts; all five press items concern the 2023 ranking. Substantively review/archive rather than simply re-date. Supply official evidence for the deck's 2026 #35 claim.

P1 — Insights renders three stale cards. The fourth seeded RPA card points to a service page rather than its article but is currently hidden by the renderer limit; correct before reuse and curate contextual content.
P1 — Legal notices need operational audits, dates, verified entity identity and client/counsel approval. These are content and credibility findings, not a legal compliance opinion.
P2 — Page meta descriptions mostly repeat titles; several titles omit Linkfields branding. Write unique purpose/benefit descriptions and confirmed canonical URLs. Contact currently lacks an H1.

P2 — Preserve Plus Jakarta Sans/Inter, British English, brand colours, unified tiles, subtle hover and sticky tabs. About, Careers and Contact have no horizontal overflow at 390px. About is roughly 14,000px tall: shorten duplication, not typography. All eight industry-image endpoints returned 200; intermittent screenshot blanks are not proven broken assets.

P2 — Remove redundant full-width social strips while retaining compact public footer links. Footer membership/certification badges need current entity-scoped evidence; logos alone do not substantiate credentials. External publisher and ATS availability was not checked because external browsing was forbidden.

reviews.summary: Reviewed all ten pages on desktop, every screenshot slice, and About, Careers and Contact on mobile. The report covers all 45 original sections plus eight proposed additions. Rework About into an evidence-backed company-trust destination and Our approach into the detailed outcome-led delivery destination; shorten repeated home content. Fix internationally blocking contact validation, recruitment links and contradictory entity/location details first. Refresh the three-post blog and historical press archive substantively, replace templated legal notices after client/counsel review, and retire the orphan legacy innovation page with a permanent redirect to Digital Transformation. No site files, services or submissions were changed; only the authorised report was written under the project.

group_findings: P1 — Retain all six routes and the fixed five portfolios. Names, colours, main sub-services and most IP mappings are deck-aligned; repetition and missing proof weaken differentiation, not the taxonomy.

P1 — Each portfolio has 11 sections and overlapping service directories. Merge original sections 3 and 4 while preserving all fixed capabilities. Talent’s section 5 should compare delivery models rather than repeat a third catalogue.

P1 — Four stats bands repeat 20+ leadership, 550+ people, 80+ clients and 20+ partners, with Platforms changing order. Talent uses 150+ consultants and 5+ data/development centres. Only common 20+ leadership is supported by the supplied deck; other counts need dated sources and definitions, not an assumption that they are false.

P1 — Deck value metrics are 95%+ reported success, up to 6× delivery speed, up to 40% development savings and up to 50% infrastructure savings. Do not paste them across portfolios as universal promises. Preserve qualifiers and require baseline, sample, period, methodology and relevant case evidence. Obtain current FT/Statista 2026 and B-BBEE supporting documents.

P1 — All five eight-industry grids are exactly identical to home in descriptions, tags, images and links. Keep the expressly requested dark photo grid and all eight sectors, but tailor and shorten each portfolio’s use cases. Illustrative needs are not client achievements.

P2 — Value-play selection is already tailored: Digital Transformation has three, Platforms/Data & AI/Cyber have two each, Talent has one. The chosen trigger/outcome/IP copy still repeats the hub; add specific portfolio contributions and evidence outputs, with cross-portfolio links.

P1 — Empty local insight/contact/social fields render global defaults, not empty sections. Four insights are configured, but all five portfolios render the same first three: two growth-news items and finance AI. The finance legacy slug returns the correct H1; the fourth RPA portfolio-link is a latent mislink, not a visible self-loop.

P1 — Services and home repeat identical portfolio cards, the full five-play table and four Why Linkfields cards; overview body is verbatim. Make Services the detailed portfolio/value-play/commercial reference and home the introduction/router. Retain required deck themes with real evidence rather than repeated assertions.

P1 — Cyber overview and SEO still advertise machine learning despite Data & AI ownership. Data & AI’s “in production today” and Cyber AI Governance’s ownership/universality need proof or qualification.

P2 — H1s and portfolio titles are present. Rendered canonical links use the sandbox forwarding host; verify deployment-origin configuration uses the approved public production domain at launch. Empty JSON canonicalUrl does not mean the rendered canonical is missing.

P2 — Desktop full-page heights including footer are 6,989px for Services and 7,764–8,691px for portfolios. At 390px, Services is 12,802px and Digital Transformation 15,483px; neither has horizontal page overflow. Reduce repeated catalogues and generic tails before shrinking typography.

P2 — Preserve portfolio accents, unified tiles, white product-logo plates, Plus Jakarta Sans/Inter, subtle hover scale and sticky active-section tabs. Consolidate service tabs and improve mobile discovery of later destinations. Do not mistake transient docking after screenshot scrolling for a proven fresh-load header defect.

P1 — Contact copy needs page-specific intent, appropriate service/demo routing, grammatical NDA wording and a confirmed response commitment. Move large social strips into the footer; the global reviewer should correct TWITTER naming and LinkedIn’s admin URL.

Evidence — All 35 desktop slices across six pages and all 13 mobile slices for Services and Digital Transformation were viewed. Initial screenshot timeouts were resolved using the prescribed shot.py with a screenshot-process font-wait bypass. No site files, builds, seeds, forms or services were changed; only the requested report was written inside the site tree.
missing_content: An approved case for each portfolio: customer/sector or approved anonymisation, challenge, scope, IP actually used, baseline/result, measurement period and publication permission.
Dated definitions and evidence for workforce/client/partner/consultant/centre counts; distinction between company age and leadership experience; current FT/Statista source and B-BBEE certificate.
Real product demos/screens, deployment/privacy facts, production-status evidence and AI Governance ownership/component/licensing boundaries.
Platform-specific delivery scope, current approved partner designations and references; clear Oracle migration/AMS scope without inventing another service family.
Security coverage/escalation/incident scope, redacted assessment evidence, current certification scope and verified regulatory applicability; no fabricated 24/7 SOC or compliance guarantees.
GCC phase ownership, acceptance criteria, knowledge transfer, IP/licensing boundaries, actual delivery-centre footprint and governance; no invented setup duration or staffing availability.
A compact illustrative integrated journey on Services and approved delivery/engagement explanations on each portfolio.
Curated, dated portfolio resources with accurate destinations and expert authors where available; approved lead routing, response commitment, service preselection and demo availability.

reviews.summary: Rework all six URLs; retire none. Retain the fixed five portfolios, product logos, unified tiles, sticky tabs and required eight-industry photo grids. Consolidate duplicate service directories, qualify unsupported scale and product claims, make evidence and industry copy portfolio-specific, curate or omit generic insights, and establish Services as the detailed buying directory rather than another home page. Reviewed every desktop slice and both selected mobile pages; all 63 existing sections and six additions are covered.

group_findings: Keep all six required service URLs and the fixed five-portfolio taxonomy. Use nine core sections: hero/sticky tabs; buyer trigger and measurable objectives; one delivery grid; tailored scenario/architecture; relevant IP/accelerators; one secure-by-design approach; approved proof; engagement/buyer questions; contextual contact. Insights are optional; social links belong in the footer.

Cloud's 17 and App modernisation's 15 sections are legacy composites, not deeper propositions. Remove whole duplicate capabilities/processes/benefits blocks, not merely words. Preserve the unified orange-accent tile model and required sticky navigation.

Remove the unsupported 60% savings and both 10x growth claims. Remove unconditional accuracy, zero-downtime, privacy and unspecified 24/7 promises. Corporate-deck metrics do not substantiate service-specific guarantees.
RPA's PARTNER RPA TOOLS visibly uses Coca-Cola and CipherWave images linked to Blue Prism and Automation Anywhere. Correct actual assets as well as alt text; partner status requires current evidence.

Integration services copies the nine-step Cloud App development grid; App modernisation rapid prototyping describes physical CAD; Quality engineering opens with garbled manufacturing-style copy. Replace contaminated content rather than polishing it.

Use tailored strategic value plays, not the whole corporate deck on every page: Modernisation & Programme Assurance for app/integration/cloud; Intelligent Operations for automation/omnichannel; AI Code Assurance for quality. Explain relevant cross-portfolio controls and actual IP roles.

Foreground Linkworks on app/integration and Testoriumz on quality; demonstrate applicable reusable artefacts elsewhere. Product logos need white plates and direct product links. Explain separate licensing and verify actual service-to-IP use.

All six pages return HTTP 200, one correct H1 and broadly relevant titles/descriptions. Canonicals currently use the ephemeral 3001 Manus host; set the approved public production domain before launch, recognising this is a local deployment artefact.

Empty source insights/contact/social fields inherit global content rather than render blank sections. The same three insight cards, virtual-coffee form and social strip repeat every tail. Limit related reading, tailor conversion and remove redundant social sections.

Desktop: all 35 slices viewed. Mobile: App modernisation 7 slices, 16,388 px high; Cloud services 9 slices, 20,507 px high. Both measured scrollWidth = viewport = 390 px, with sticky tabs docking around y=72 px and updating aria-current. No horizontal overflow was found in these checks. Excessive card stacks and tiny raster-process text—not broken responsiveness—are the principal mobile issues. Sequential retries resolved three confirmed screenshot timeouts without site/service changes.
missing_content: Approved scoped case per service: business trigger, initial estate/process, work performed, actual IP/accelerators, baseline, period, measured outcomes and permission. Anonymised references must disclose sector/scope; invent no clients, figures or guarantees.
Approved Linkworks/Testoriumz logos, UI screenshots, demo availability and precise service-to-IP fit; examples of actual reusable accelerator artefacts and reuse boundaries.

Current supported-platform/tool scope, correct vendor assets and partner/certification evidence including issuer, designation, validity and display permission. Correct RPA customer-logo/tool-link mismatches immediately.

Managed cloud/automation/quality responsibility matrices, hours/regions, response versus restoration SLAs, exclusions, recovery requirements, reporting cadence and ownership. Confirm the global form response commitment before publishing within 24 hours.

Service-specific buyer answers: app estate/coexistence/refactor decisions; RPA API-versus-bot/exceptions/credentials/AI approvals/net benefit; integration contracts/reconciliation/failures/ownership; WhatsApp provider model/opt-in/data/channels/templates/handover/commerce boundaries; quality pipeline/AI code/gates/licence-versus-service; cloud readiness/landing zones/cost/shared responsibility/recovery/managed scope.

Secure-by-design evidence throughout delivery: access/data controls, security and test gates, human approval where relevant, release evidence and operating ownership. Align with Cyber Security/Data & AI without inventing regulatory coverage or certifications.

reviews.summary: Reviewed all six pages, all 35 desktop slices and 16 mobile slices across App modernisation and Cloud services. Keep the six required URLs but rework them around one nine-section, outcome-led template. The report covers all 73 original sections plus 22 proposed additions. Priority fixes are unsupported 60%/10x claims, incorrect RPA vendor logos, copied cloud-development content on Integration services, garbled legacy copy, duplicate capability/process/benefits blocks, and buried or absent Linkfields IP. No site files were changed except the requested report; no builds, seeds, service commands or form submissions were run.

group_findings: P1 — Header · Solutions mega menu: retire the parallel “Solutions” taxonomy while preserving the five Services portfolios. ERP/CRM platforms belong in IEP; iPaaS belongs within Digital Transformation → Integration services; RPA belongs in Automation & RPA. Linkworks retains its single product page.

P1 — Header · Testorium Z: remove the unexplained external shortcut from Solutions. Use “testoriumz” and /products-and-accelerators/testoriumz under Products & Accelerators/Quality engineering; offer a clearly labelled external demo/product link there.

P1 — Footer · Solutions column and IEP inbound links: remove the legacy column or replace it with Enterprise platforms linking final destinations. Update header, footer, IEP hub, cards, breadcrumbs and CTAs together. The current “SAP S/4HANA” menu opens an H1 “SAP HANA” page.

P1 — SAP consolidation: no current SAP sub-page warrants independence. Preserve verified acquisition/carve-out, template-rollout, Fiori, EHS/commerce/planning, migration/reconciliation and deployment-specific HANA/Basis scope. Do not retain generic data filler or marketing-agency copy wholesale.

P1 — Terminology/proof: use SAP S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics 365, SAP BW/4HANA and British English; distinguish HANA database operations from ERP transformation. Have the technical lead refresh Hybris, SAP Model Company, HANA Live, TDI/appliance and ALM/Solution Manager scope without inventing lifecycle deadlines. Withdraw latest-release/pioneering/effortless-compliance claims, 60% savings and unverified credentials/statistics.

P2 — Platform pattern: buyer outcome/fit → confirmed apps/deployment → concrete delivery → controlled implementation/adoption → architecture/IP/assurance → evidence → contextual enquiry. Keep unified blue IEP tiles, white logo plates and required sticky tabs. Do not repeat entire portfolios, industries or corporate metrics everywhere.

P2 — Visual/mobile: typography/navy tiles are broadly coherent, but closed accordions hide detail, long headings impair scanning and generic globals dominate thin pages. Zoho, AMS, ERP and SAP all have document width 390px at a 390px viewport, without horizontal overflow. Keep intentionally scrolling tabs, fix mismatched IDs, shorten essays and use platform/workflow or delivery imagery with permission.

P2 — Shared conversion/globals: replace virtual-coffee/Submit wording with platform-priority discussions and a verified response process. Keep one contextual form and relevant optional guidance. reviews.summary: Retire the legacy Solutions taxonomy and ERP hub. Move SAP S/4HANA, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Odoo and Salesforce into IEP with direct permanent redirects. Consolidate all five SAP sub-pages into one SAP platform offer plus Platform migration & AMS, preserving verified unique capability rather than legacy copy. Zoho needs application specificity and proof; AMS needs a genuine cross-platform operating model. Remove unrelated advertising, unsupported metrics and misleading terminology. Reviewed all 12 page JSON files and all desktop screenshot slices, plus mobile slices for Zoho, AMS, ERP and SAP. Report contains 92 original-section assessments and 17 additions. No site files or services were changed.

group_findings: P1 — Keep all four mandated Data & AI services and URLs. Strategy decides investment/governance; Agentic AI delivers grounded answers and bounded workflow actions; Data platforms delivers dependable sources/platform/reporting; ML delivers evaluated prediction/scoring/forecasting. Fix duplicate copy, not the fixed taxonomy.

P1 — Delete '10x faster operational growth', guaranteed ROI and guaranteed accuracy. The deck does not substantiate them; its 'Up to 6×' technology-delivery metric cannot be relabelled operational growth or model performance.

P1 — Separate services, proprietary software and reusable accelerators. Add relevant compact links rather than repeated catalogue grids: Agentic → textIQ/FinSight/EduPilot/workflow IP; analytics → Power BI + AI/ML and financial-context FinSight; ML → Predictive Analytics and decision-relevant Digital Twin. Product availability does not imply inclusion or universal fit.
P1 — Explain the boundary between AI strategy & governance advice, Cyber Security AI security & GRC and AI Governance gateway/guardrails software, with ownership and delivery hand-offs.

P1 — Machine learning correctly belongs under Data & AI; the old Cyber Security route was verified as a 308 redirect. Security detection should remain one cross-portfolio use case, not the defining purpose.

P2 — Standard specialist template: outcome-led hero/required sticky tabs → buyer trigger → deliverables → tailored process/acceptance → relevant service/software/IP route → one proof example → specific CTA/contextual form. Keep unified purple-accent tiles, white product logo plates and subtle hover expansion.

P2 — Blank insights/contact/social JSON fields inherit visible global content; they are not empty placeholders. The renderer displays three of the four global insight records. Remove repeated specialist-page corporate news, tailor the form and merge social promotion into the footer.

P1 — Shared LinkedIn destination https://www.linkedin.com/company/40661516/admin/feed/posts/ is an administrator path; the global owner should supply the approved public company URL. Modernise TWITTER to X. Treat 2023 FT coverage as historical, not 2026 evidence.

P2 — Demonstrate one integrated partner through actual integration, security validation and operational ownership, not repeated five-portfolio/eight-industry grids. Use relevant client-confirmed deck commercial models; do not invent package durations, prices, SLAs or universal software inclusion.

P2 — All four inspected pages have one meaningful H1 and relevant title/meta descriptions; Data platforms needs metadata rewriting. Local canonicals use the temporary forwarded 3001 hostname because seed canonicalUrl is blank. Check intended public-domain canonicals before deployment; this does not establish a current public-site fault.

P2 — Full-page captures contain an Agentic duplicate pinned row and displaced Data header, potentially scrolling/capture artefacts. Verify stable viewport docking/scroll-to-top/active-state/anchor-offset behaviour before logging implementation bugs; preserve the required sticky bar.

P2 — All 15 desktop and seven priority mobile slices were viewed. Strategy/Agentic mobile DOM states had scrollWidth 390; captured heights were 6,801/8,628 px. Retain readable stacked tiles/accordions, but remove repeated cards, tall generic news and the extra social band; expose process outputs without opening every accordion. Additions with the same position are inserted before that original JSON section, in listed order.
missing_content: P1 — Client-approved service scope and actual artefacts: roadmap/prioritisation/governance roles; agent retrieval/tools/evaluation/handover; platform/pipeline/Power BI/quality responsibilities; ML baseline/evaluation/deployment/monitoring. Proposed structures must not become unverified capability claims.

P2 — One permissioned relevant proof story per service: challenge, scope, baseline, period, metric definition and limits. Supply redacted roadmap/control matrix, AI trace/evaluation, data-flow/dashboard and model card/evaluation. Label illustrative samples; never fabricate clients or outcomes.

P1 — Software/accelerator fit, feature limits and readiness evidence: real screens/demo context, deployment/integration requirements and licence/engagement route. Demo availability is not proof of enterprise production deployment; reusable IP is not automatically SaaS.

P2 — Cross-portfolio responsibility map covering policies, access/guardrails, security testing, systems integration, release approval and operations. Confirm applicability/evidence before citing POPIA, sector regulation or certifications; no blanket compliance guarantees.
P2 — Supported data/AI platform expertise and current partner/certification evidence before adding badges or technology logos; no invented hyperscaler/model/tool wall.

P2 — Approved commercial entry points, project acceptance criteria, managed-operation ownership, dedicated-team roles and service-specific first-conversation promise. Validate the inherited 24-hour response commitment and replace the NDA/privacy overclaim.

reviews.summary: Rework all four pages while retaining their URLs and the fixed sub-service taxonomy. The visual family is consistent and readable, but enterprise differentiation is weakened by generic deliverables, overlapping service boundaries, unlinked proprietary products, missing regulatory evidence and an undefined security-operations delivery model. Correct Vector X to VectorX, separate products from accelerators, define supported scope and operating responsibilities, replace unrelated global sections with verified proof, and tailor conversion. All desktop slices and mobile slices for AI security & GRC and Security operations were reviewed; screenshots are under /tmp/review/cyber-subservices/. No site files or services were changed.

group_findings: P1 — Keep the fixed five portfolios and four mandated sub-services. Consolidate Staff augmentation and Managed teams into directly addressable sections on Specialist talent & managed teams. Preserve exact engagement labels, build destinations before retirement, implement permanent redirects, update navigation/internal links/sitemap and validate sticky-header anchor landings.

P1 — GCC BOT already uses one URL in both the sub-service list and ENGAGEMENT MODELS. This is valid dual classification, not two physical duplicate pages. Keep one canonical BOT destination; do not create a model clone. Keep GCC strategy & setup separately for pre-launch blueprint decisions with a clear BOT hand-off.

P1 — Separate skills supplied, delivery accountability and commercial terms. Staff augmentation/managed teams/BOT explain delivery direction or operation. Fixed Price, Time & Materials, Managed Service, Dedicated Team and Outcome-Based are commercial choices. Outcome-led pods do not automatically mean outcome-based fees or infrastructure managed services.

P1 — Remove every '10x faster operational growth' claim. Do not substitute 'Up to 6×', which concerns differently scoped technology delivery. Obtain dated evidence/definitions for 5+ centres, 550+ people, 150+ consultants and Hyderabad before restoring GCC proof statements.

P2 — Use a compact common journey: outcome-led hero/contextual CTA → scope/best fit → deliverables → responsibility/process gates → relevant IP/accelerators → approved evidence → contextual enquiry. Keep sticky tabs, yellow accents, British English and unified tiles; do not repeat full industry/value-play grids on each sub-page.

P2 — Null process images leave substantial empty desktop columns and all accordions are initially collapsed. Expose essential outputs and responsibility summaries without clicks. Use full-width processes or meaningful approved artefacts; align darker outline-led flow cards with unified yellow capability tiles.

P2 — Both mobile-priority pages have scrollWidth 390 at a 390px viewport: no horizontal overflow found. Approximately 8,000px journeys contain repetitive stacked model/capability cards and news/social tails. Shorten through consolidation/removal, not smaller type or removal of requested scrolling tabs.

P2 — Remove generic Insights & Updates and standalone social banners here. Historic FT 2023 news may remain in news but is neither talent/GCC proof nor the deck's 2026 ranking evidence. Global social data uses TWITTER and a LinkedIn admin URL. Correct public destinations, NDA grammar and the response-time policy globally.

P2 — Each rendered page has one meaningful H1, descriptive metadata and no duplicate HTML IDs. reviews.summary: Reviewed all six page JSONs, every desktop screenshot slice, and both mobile-priority pages. Keep the four deck-mandated sub-service destinations, but merge staff augmentation and managed teams into anchored sections on Specialist talent & managed teams. Keep one GCC BOT page serving both its sub-service and engagement-model roles. Replace legacy IT-support/team-administration copy, remove unsupported 10x claims, substantiate GCC footprint figures, and make deliverables, accountability, embedded IP and transfer terms concrete. The report covers all 54 existing sections and seven proposed additions; no site files or services were changed.

group_findings: Preserve the top-level Products & Accelerators destination, five fixed service portfolios, approved logos on white plates, colour-accent/unified tiles and sticky tabs. Four portfolios contain software; do not invent a Talent Advisory & GCC product for symmetry.

P1: Most capability cards paraphrase their titles. Use a shared enterprise product narrative: buyer problem/fit → real capabilities → software screens/workflow → approved use case/evidence → enterprise fit → contextual demo/enquiry. Keep pages compact; do not append repeated corporate value-play, industry or global-insight grids.

P1: Reconcile “Software we own” with AI Governance’s Portkey + Opik. Client must identify proprietary layer, third-party components/licences and operational responsibility while retaining the fixed name and Cyber Security placement.

P1: Linkworks and VajraX mention licence/subscription/SaaS while other detail pages lack buying clarity. Licence/subscription are commercial models; SaaS/customer-managed are deployment choices. Publish availability per product, not a universal promise. Separate reusable accelerator engagement terms.

P1: Every form defaults to generic service language and “Submit”. Preserve product and enquiry intent, make phone optional, explain the actual next step and privacy terms. Verify “within 24 hours” and remove the absolute NDA/privacy promise.
P1: testoriumz’s “VISIT TESTORIUMZ” tab targets an absent visit-testoriumz ID. Repair the target; existing delivery/contact anchors are present. Preserve the requested sticky-tab behaviour.

P2: The hub uses internal product routes. testoriumz.com is a product-site link; textIQ/FinSight/VajraX use lfidemo.com subdomains and EduPilot uses lfiai.com. Rendered external links correctly use new tabs with noopener/noreferrer. Clearly distinguish product website from public/sample demo, disclose access and safe-data rules, provide a local guided-demo fallback and maintain consistent Linkfields ownership/support identity. External destination health/content was not audited in this local-only review.

P2: Linkworks appears under two portfolios appropriately; identify it as one product with two applications, not nine unique products. Align FinSight’s banking-only and EduPilot’s institution-only wording to the broader deck propositions or obtain a documented scope decision.

P2: Each page has a title/meta description and one rendered H1. Product-purpose title wording could improve Linkworks, testoriumz and AI Governance. Rendered canonicals use the temporary 3001 forwarding host; production must emit verified corporate-domain canonicals.

P2: Merge the repeated oversized social strip into the footer. Retain coherent visual styling, but branded thematic imagery cannot substitute for genuine product screens, architecture and proof. Product heroes lack their approved logo plates.

P2: All nine desktop pages and all 28 slices were inspected; hub/testoriumz mobile and all eight slices were inspected. Both mobile pages have scrollWidth = viewport = 390 and tabs dock beneath the header when scrolled. reviews.summary: Retain the hub and all eight product URLs, but rework them as enterprise evaluation pages rather than category teasers. All nine desktop pages and all slices were reviewed, plus hub and testoriumz mobile. No site changes, redirects or taxonomy changes are recommended.

group_findings: P1: Preserve all five named accelerator pages and the fixed five portfolios. Explain the deck distinction ‘Software we own. Accelerators we reuse.’ with actual assets and adaptation boundaries, not a product-like brochure template.

P1: ‘WHAT'S INSIDE’ consistently lists capabilities rather than a verified pre-built inventory. Client-supplied artefacts, prerequisites, delivery outputs and confirmed commercial/ownership terms are needed to establish reusable IP.

P1 shared-form handoff: ‘Products & accelerators (licence / SaaS)’ conflates reusable delivery IP with independently licensed products. Give accelerator enquiries a separate route and identify the current accelerator. Existing source-path tracking should be preserved.

P1 shared-form handoff: Read-only source inspection confirms mandatory telephone validation permits only SA local or +27 formats. Support international or optional telephone and align server validation. No form was submitted.

P1 global-link/launch handoff: LinkedIn points to https://www.linkedin.com/company/40661516/admin/feed/posts/ and needs a client-confirmed public URL. All five reviewed renderings emit temporary manus.computer canonicals with empty JSON canonical fields and noIndex false; correct public-domain canonicals at launch and prevent preview indexing. This is an environment finding, not a claim about the existing public website.

P2: The renderer correctly hides each current accelerator; there is no visible self-link bug. The four remaining full sibling cards still repeat the hub. Keep the comprehensive catalogue at /products-and-accelerators; use tailored portfolio/industry links and one or two complementary accelerator tiles on detail pages.

P2: Retain Power BI and Predictive Analytics as separate pages, explicitly explaining model-versus-reporting roles. Connect workflow to Intelligent Operations and Delivery accelerators to programme assurance, regulated readiness and embedded-IP GCC contexts without unverified bundling.

P2: Preserve unified navy tiles, broadly relevant imagery and sticky tabs. Both checked mobile pages have scrollWidth = clientWidth = 390, but the sibling catalogue creates a long detour and the initial contact tab is off-screen. Add visible hero CTAs, condense related links, merge the contact-page CTA strip into the local form and remove duplicate social strips.

P2 shared-copy handoff: Replace virtual-coffee copy with relevant assessment invitations; change the NDA sentence to ‘Where required, we can agree an NDA before reviewing confidential information.’ Verify the 24-hour response promise, add visible privacy guidance and labels, and use a multiline enquiry field.

P2: Delivery sequences are sensibly decision-led but need named accepted outputs and an explanation of reused versus new work. Do not apply corporate ‘Up to 6×’ or cost-saving figures to individual accelerators without scoped evidence; preserve the existing relevant H1s, unique titles and meaningful meta descriptions.
missing_content: Verified reusable-IP inventories with real artefacts, supported inputs/platforms and version/support status; identify what is pre-built and what remains bespoke for each accelerator.

Confirmed commercial availability, product licence dependencies, ownership, client access/handover/reuse rights and maintenance/support responsibility, separating accelerator adoption from software SaaS/licensing.

Accelerator-specific readiness and secure-by-design boundaries: data/history/labels, access, hosting/integration, refresh/latency, permissions, calibration/validation, human approvals, audit evidence and acceptance criteria.

One approved artefact or clearly labelled demonstration per accelerator, with permission for attribution and measured proof including scope, baseline, measurement period and comparator; no invented clients, metrics, certifications or partner status.
Time-to-value evidence showing the first usable deliverable, reused versus new work, delivery assumptions and a documented comparison before publishing timings or improvement metrics.
Client confirmation of portfolio, industry, strategic-value-play and proprietary-product relationships, expressed as contextual links without implied product bundling or fictitious accelerator packs.

reviews.summary: Rework all five pages while retaining their URLs, the client-required taxonomy, unified tiles and sticky tabs. The deck-aligned capabilities are clear, but the pages do not demonstrate what is pre-built, what remains bespoke or how reuse changes time-to-value. Replace the repeated sibling catalogue with contextual portfolio/industry links, add verified artefacts and readiness boundaries, and correct shared enquiry classification and international telephone validation. All five desktop pages and Predictive Analytics plus Delivery accelerators on mobile were captured successfully; all 26 slices were inspected. Review was read-only apart from the authorised report and screenshot files.

group_findings: P1 — Manufacturing’s rendered meta description falsely describes Linkfields as a manufacturing company. Telecom’s meta description merely repeats its title. All nine pages return HTTP 200 and have one meaningful H1.

P1 — Only Education has a product/accelerator link in its page body, to EduPilot. The other industry pages fail to connect relevant proprietary software and reusable accelerators to their use cases. Telecom and Manufacturing link only automation, advisory and app modernisation.

P2 — Keep the fixed eight-industry taxonomy, all nine reviewed URLs, the dark ‘Industries we know deeply’ photo-card grid including Public Sector and Education, the five portfolios and sticky section tabs. No retirement or redirect is recommended.

P2 — Standardise detail pages: hero → concise context/optional sector routes → compact exact-taxonomy portfolio map → visible industry workflows → selected software/accelerators → evidence → contextual enquiry. Move the premature blue CTA beside the final form. Building-tools should explain delivery; specialisation should explain industry work, not repeat the same concepts.

P2 — Building-tools already uses the navy rounded/accent tile treatment; refine it rather than introducing another visual system. Replace the specialisation carousel with visible unified workflow tiles. Manufacturing needs the most pruning: eight items include overlapping quality and planning concepts.

P2 — Apply British English and consistent sentence case. Replace ‘Our Specialization’/‘OUR SPECIALIZATION’ with ‘What we deliver’ or ‘Our specialisation’; edit Telecom’s Digitalization/organizations/skillful and Manufacturing’s Revolutionizing/customized/Optimize/minimize/analyze/digitization. Preserve component identifiers and the fixed taxonomy.

P2 — Empty local insight/form/social fields inherit global content. Three generic insight cards render in a desktop grid and stack on mobile. Global JSON also contains a fourth RPA card not visible in these captures; its configured destination is a service hub, not an article. Curate relevant articles, remove irrelevant global news from detail pages and remove the standalone social strip while retaining footer socials. Correct the LinkedIn admin/feed URL.

P1 — No industry-delivery case, measured baseline/result or regulated-deployment control artefact appears in this group. Narrow claims or request client evidence for healthcare outcomes, manufacturing compliance, financial risk/compliance, public accessibility and education product features. Proposed IP applicability is not proof of sector deployments.

P2 — Blank seed canonicalUrl values render absolute canonicals on the supplied preview hostname. Configure final public-domain canonicals at release; do not hard-code localhost or the sandbox hostname.

P2 — Historical 2023 FT news is not a current 2026 credential. Keep it dated in the archive; request the original source for the deck’s #35 FT & Statista Africa Growth Ranking 2026 and current B-BBEE/certification scope before elevating them as proof.

reviews.summary: Completed the read-only review of all nine pages, all 72 original sections and 19 proposed additions. Inspected 34 desktop slices and 10 mobile slices. Retain all industry URLs and the required hub grid, but rebuild the proposition around industry workflows, integrated portfolios, selected Linkfields software/accelerators and evidence. Fix Manufacturing’s false business description and Telecom’s opaque legacy copy first. The newer pages have useful scope but repeat it across service cards and a one-slide-at-a-time specialisation carousel.

group_findings: P1: Publish substantial #banking, #insurance and #fintech modules on BFSI and #mining and #oil-gas modules on Energy & Mining before permanently redirecting the five children. Update umbrella sector cards, header sector chips, internal links and sitemap entries to the parent anchors; canonicalise to the parent pages without fragments. Preserve the eight-industry grid and five fixed portfolios.

P1: Banking and Insurance rendered meta descriptions misidentify Linkfields as a bank and insurer. Correct them immediately while migration is pending. Fintech, Mining and Oil & Gas descriptions are title-only. All five have one sector H1.

P1: Remove unsupported compliance, financial-advice, fraud-prevention, personalised-coverage, safety, no-downtime, profit and market-share assurances. The deck establishes capabilities and IP, not proof of sector deployments or regulatory approval.

P2: The identical Building tools that endure block and listeners-and-leaders banner should not survive consolidation. Use one outcome-led flow per umbrella: overview, named sector outcome tiles, relevant services/IP/accelerators, approved evidence, contextual engagement/contact, optional curated resources and footer.

P2: The large specialisation panel hides all but one description; other descriptions are absent from the initial server-rendered page. Prefer visible, scan-friendly unified tiles. Keyboard selection works on inspected Banking/Insurance tabs, so the component should not be labelled non-functional. Mining's active checklist/laptop image is unrelated to operational monitoring.

P2: Preserve the client-required sticky tabs but repair return-to-top state. Insurance's desktop screenshot shows both docked and hero tab sets with GET IN TOUCH highlighted at the top; a read-only return-to-top check reproduced two sets on Banking and Insurance. Hand this to the shared component owner and retest fast/smooth scrolling and reduced motion.

P1/P2: Shared social links use LinkedIn /admin/feed/posts/ and need a verified public URL. Remove redundant child social strips. Historical 2023 rankings belong in Company/news or a single clearly dated trust treatment; obtain approved 2026 ranking evidence rather than implying the historical card is false.

P2: Empty page insights/form/social fields inherit global content. Four global insight entries result in three visible cards here; title/destination fidelity needs review, including an RPA article entry pointing to a service page. Tested local links return 200. Keep one parent form with sector context, precise confidentiality wording, confirmed response commitments and privacy guidance. No form submission or backend validation was tested.

P2: All desktop slices and Banking/Mining mobile slices were inspected. Both mobile documents measured 390 px wide at a 390 px viewport with no page overflow. Rendered canonicals currently use the sandbox forwarding host; confirm the true public production domain at deployment. No builds, seeds, service changes or site edits were performed.

P2: No supplied analytics proves independent child-page search demand. Record landing-page/query and inbound-link history before migration. Reopen a standalone sector page only when distinct buyer need, substantial approved delivery proof and demonstrable demand justify it.
missing_content: P1: Approved attributable or anonymised evidence per sector, identifying the problem, Linkfields scope, integrations, controls, acceptance criteria and baseline/measurement period for any outcomes. Do not invent clients, savings, uptime, fraud rates or certifications.

P1: Explicit human-review, data-access, model-validation and audit-evidence boundaries for financial-services workflows; separation of enterprise IT/analytics from industrial process-control and safety-critical responsibilities for resource operations. Confirm applicable requirements with legal/security owners for actual scope and target markets.

P2: Approved walkthroughs connecting named Linkfields products and reusable accelerators to real sector workflows, prerequisites, configured/custom-built components and operating limits. Distinguish products, accelerators and third-party platforms.

P2: A concrete buyer starting point explaining how an initial discussion or scoped assessment identifies workflow priorities, data/integration dependencies, controls, acceptance criteria and suitable project/managed-service/dedicated-team engagement. Do not invent free offers, fixed durations, prices or guarantees.

P2: Real approved architecture/process diagrams or anonymised dashboards with sensitive information removed; verified terminal/SAP IS-Oil module/version experience and partner evidence if those claims remain.
P2: Migration evidence including landing-page/search-query history, incoming links and confirmed public canonical domain; approved current ranking citation and verified public LinkedIn URL.

reviews.summary: Merge all five legacy sub-industry pages into substantial, directly addressable sector sections within BFSI and Energy & Mining, then permanently redirect the old URLs. The umbrellas already contain almost all useful sector topics; the children add repeated service copy and unsupported assurances rather than specialist proof. Correct the Banking/Insurance business descriptions immediately, remove unsupported fraud/compliance/advice/safety/profit claims, and add approved sector evidence with named Linkfields IP and clear operating boundaries. All desktop slices and Banking/Mining mobile slices were inspected; no site files were modified and no forms were submitted.

group_findings: P1: Separate outcome-led Solutions from capability-led Services while preserving the five fixed portfolios and Products & Accelerators top-level. Eliminate mixed vendor/RPA/iPaaS/product duplication in navigation and footer.
P1: Both contact client and server require a phone matching only 0 plus nine digits or +27 plus nine digits. This blocks the global audience. Make telephone optional and internationally validated.
P1: Contact has no H1 and contradicts the deck: Botswana appears, UK is absent and South Africa telephone numbers conflict. Obtain client confirmation rather than guessing addresses/numbers.

P1: Four global insight records become three rendered cards without dates. Two promote the 2023 ranking; finance/RPA records dated 2024 contain already-expired forecasts. Replace promotion with verified current proof and expert insight, not cosmetic date updates.
P1: LinkedIn uses an admin-feed URL in both social locations. Correct it and consolidate social promotion in the footer.

P1: Logos and deck performance claims need auditable current entity/scope/validity and baseline/method evidence before public promotion. The supplied deck does not itself substantiate public numerical outcomes.

P1: The 404 needs branded recovery links. Repeat screenshots, browser navigation and three later curl GETs returned 404/noindex; the initial 200 was not reproduced and should be treated as an observation for cold/cache verification, not a confirmed persistent soft-404 defect.

P2: Preserve the globe, sticky tabs, portfolio accents, product logos, dark eight-industry photo tiles and unified surfaces. Shorten repeated catalogues and recruitment/social distractions. Home is especially long on mobile; all four checked pages have scrollWidth 390 at viewport 390, with no measured horizontal overflow.
Careers is intentionally a direct /careers link with no mega menu. Membership/ISO groups are badge-only, not empty columns. They need accurate classification and evidence, not filler links.

Delivery caveat: /home/ubuntu/linkfields/docs/review/13-global.md has not yet been written. Complete draft decisions are at /tmp/review/global/result.json and screenshots/scripts at /tmp/review/global/. Parent should render the final decisions to the requested Markdown path and use this final JSON's corrected 404 status wording.

Proposed steps, subject to client process confirmation: 'We’ll route your enquiry to the relevant portfolio specialist'; 'Where needed, we’ll agree an NDA before you share confidential information'; 'We’ll clarify your priorities and agree the next step'. Group all requested sub-services under the five portfolios, separate product/licence interest and replace Others with 'Not sure — help me choose'. Make phone optional/international in client and server, add company/work email, persistent labels, textarea and linked privacy notice. Verify lead storage, routing and acknowledgement through a separately authorised test; no form was submitted in this review.
